references.text: Earlier command to eat unleavened bread for seven days, with specific dates given in verse 18.
Repeats the command to eat unleavened bread for seven days during the Feast of Unleavened Bread.
Describes the Feast of Unleavened Bread in the month of Abib, celebrated for seven days.
Command to observe the Feast of Unleavened Bread for seven days in the month of Abib.
Specifies the exact date of Passover on the fourteenth day of the first month, followed by the Feast of Unleavened Bread.
Confirms the timing of Passover on the fourteenth day of the month, at evening.
Passover on the fourteenth day of the first month, with a feast and unleavened bread starting from the fifteenth day.
Command to eat unleavened bread for seven days in remembrance of the exodus from Egypt.
Six days of unleavened bread, with a holy assembly on the seventh day.
The Israelites celebrated the Feast of Unleavened Bread for seven days during King Hezekiah's reform.
Passover celebration and the Feast of Unleavened Bread for seven days during the time of King Josiah.
Celebration of the Feast of Unleavened Bread for seven days after returning from exile.
Ezekiel's prophecy about Passover on the fourteenth day of the first month, with a seven-day celebration using unleavened bread.
The first day of the Feast of Unleavened Bread, when the disciples prepared the Passover meal for Jesus.
Passover and the Feast of Unleavened Bread were two days away when they planned to arrest Jesus.
The first day of the Festival of Unleavened Bread, when the Passover lamb was sacrificed.
The Day of Unleavened Bread came, when the Passover lamb had to be sacrificed.
Peter's arrest took place during the Festival of Unleavened Bread.
Paul sailed from Philippi after the days of Unleavened Bread.
Christ as our Passover lamb and the call to celebrate with unleavened bread, symbolizing purity and truth.
Leviticus 23:6 specifies that the seven-day Festival of Unleavened Bread formally begins on the 15th day, immediately after the Passover lamb.
Numbers 28:17 confirms the start of the festival on the 15th day, completing the timeframe from the evening of the 14th to the evening of the 21st in Exodus.
Exodus 13:6 clarifies the duration (seven days) and notes that the seventh day is a sacred assembly concluding the period.
Numbers 9:11 presents the exception rule for celebrating in the second month, highlighting both flexibility and the firmness of the requirement relative to the main rule in Exodus.
Exodus 13:7 expands on the command by requiring the complete removal of leaven from the entire land during the seven days.
